“I wasted ₹50,000 on ads before realizing this one mistake was killing every campaign.”

Most businesses think their ads fail because they need better targeting.

But targeting wasn’t my problem.

People were seeing the ad — they just weren’t stopping to watch it.

So I changed one thing.

Instead of starting with ‘We help businesses grow online,’ I started with the exact problem my customer was experiencing.

‘Getting clicks but zero customers?’

Same product. Same audience. Same ad budget.

The only major change was the first three seconds.

And suddenly, people actually stayed long enough to understand the offer.

Before you increase your ad budget, fix your hook first.

Save this and test three different hooks on your next campaign.

scripts.title: You're probably trying to fix the wrong...
scripts.scriptText:
You're probably trying to fix the wrong part of your Reel.

If your views keep dying, don't change the entire video yet. Check what happens in the first 3 seconds.

Here's the test: open your last 5 Reels and watch only the beginning—with the sound off.

Ask yourself: would someone who doesn't know me immediately understand why they should keep watching?

If the answer is no, check these 3 things.

First: remove the greeting. “Hey guys, welcome back” uses your most valuable seconds without giving the viewer a reason to stay.

Second: replace the topic with tension. Don't say, “Here are 3 Instagram tips.” Say what could be going wrong and make the viewer want the explanation.

Third: make the outcome specific. “Grow your Instagram” is vague. Tell viewers exactly what they're about to learn, avoid, or achieve.

Before you create another Reel, fix just those first 3 seconds.

Save this, test it on your next post, and compare the difference.

Stop blaming the Instagram algorithm. Your first 3 seconds might be the real reason people aren't watching your Reels.

Mistake two: giving away the topic without creating a reason to keep watching. Don't say, “Here are some Instagram tips.” Create a gap: tell me what's going wrong—but make me stay to discover why.

Mistake three: asking for a follow before earning attention. Give viewers something useful first, then give them a reason to come back.

Here's your test: rewrite only the first 3 seconds of your next Reel. Remove the greeting, lead with the problem, and create one unanswered question.

Save this before you post your next Reel—and compare how long people actually keep watching.
